GCXXIII. obwaltenden Streit gütlich bei. My Oldrzich z Rozmberka a Jan syn geho odtudz wyznawame tiemto listem obecznie przedewssemi, ktoz gey vzrzie anebo cztucze slysseti budu, ze duostoyny kniez Pawel opat Wissobrodsky s gedne a sluwutny Waczlaw Talafus z Dobrzan sedienim w Porzieczij z sirany 278 druhe prosyli nas, abychme niektere z nassie raddy mezy nie wyslali k ohledanij czesty a ginych wieczy, o kterez spolu wruozniczy byli gsu. A my znamenawsse gich obogich dobrowolne prosby a hodne y poslali sme k nim a mezy nie slowutneho punossi Jana Rusla z Czemin raddu a wierneho nasseho mileho, aby 1y wiec/.y mezy nimi ohledal a ge otto nassim rozkazanim a moczij rozdieli!. A kdyz swrrhudotczeny Jan Rus mezy nie przygel, a ty wieczy ohledal s ginymi dubrymi lidmi, kterziz gse suobu slranu take przitom byli y rozilielil a smluwil ge suobugich stran dobru wol.j takto, jakoz w dole psano stogi. Item najprwe o tu czestu, kteraz gde od Bors- sowa przes rzeku mymo rybniczek na koru k Porzieczij a k Dubij a od tad dale k Plawu a k lukmn, kterez na Boru lezie, gestu gsu ty luky Borssowskych, y bke o tu czestu, kteraz od rybniezka gde skrze Dubie k Roznowu a k Budiegiowiczom prosyli su za tie obo^i czestie wssic/.kui hospodarzy z Borssowa Talafusa pro buoli a pro matku bozij, aby giui tiech czest dal poziwati, aby tudy mohli s wozy y s konmy gezdieti, kromye dobytka s stadem nemagy houitii a on gym gest dal swobodu ne zprawa, alle z dobre wuole a z gich proslry, na tiech czestach mieti takowu, yakoz sie swrchupisse, a on sam y geho wssichni buduczij y kazdy ten, kteryzby na tom dworze w Porzieczij sediel , to tak tez drzeti, magi wiecznie a sobie na tom neprzekazeti. A kniez opat ma geho lidem z Porzieczie y z wescze nebraniti lesuow, czozby mohli sobie na y.adij vnesti, neb na kolesiech, aneb na saiiknch zimie samotiez bez konij westi; a Talufus a geho lide z wescze y namiestczi geho budu mocti pasti y Irawu zieti w knieze opatowie lese tak, yakoz gsu prwe pasly y /eli od starodawna. Take kniez opat bude moczi b.ky sobie dieluti, kdezby chtiel w swych lesiech, a ty kazati ohraditi, a Talafus a geho lide y buduczij nemagij gemu na tom przekazeti. Take gest d;rle. mezy nimi wypowiedieno a vmluweno o niekaky (sic) ostrow, kteryz lezij wedle Borssowskych luk, aby Borssowsstij tubo o>trowu poziwali potawad, yskoz gest meze vdielana na gedne welike wrbie, a kamen meznij gest wsazen a od tee meze kniez opat a Borssowsstij magij tee zaloky poziwati, czoz na horu wodu topi; a T.rlafus dole pod tu mezy toho o^trowu a zatoky te ma poziwati potad, yakuz meze vkazuge a rzeky ohoge strany magij spolu pozi wati, jakoz od starodawna to bylo. Take gestli zeby swrchupsanym czesty gezdiecz na obilij kde kteru sskodu Talafusowi vcziuili, o tu 279 sskodu magij Borssowsstij Talafusa neb gebo buduczich odbyti, jakzby dwa dubra czlowieky rzekla. A ty wsseczkny wieczy swrchu- psane slibili gsu dobrowolnye oboge strany cztnie, wiernie a krze- stiansky z drzeti a zachowati podeczlij a pod wieru bez przerussenie wsselikeho. entries.english:
1453, 24 August. Krumau. Ulrich and Johann von Rosenberg amicably settle the dispute between Hohenfurt Abbey and Wenzel Talafus concerning a road and passage across the Vltava from the village of Payreschau to Porte.

The original charter is in Old Czech, and its surviving transcription is substantially corrupted and partly illegible. The readable portions record that Abbot Pavel of Hohenfurt and Wenzel Talafus of Dobřany, resident at Porziecz, asked Ulrich and Johann to send a member of their council to inspect and settle their disputes. The Rosenbergs sent their councillor and retainer Jan Rusl of Czemin. Following his inspection with other trustworthy men present on both sides, an agreement was reached as follows: the people of Borssow were granted use of two roads, one running from Borssow past the river and fishpond toward the court at Porziecz and onward to Plaw and the meadows on the Borssow side; the other running from the fishpond through Dubie toward Roznow and Budegowitz. They were permitted to use these roads with carts and horses, but not to drive livestock in herds. The agreement further regulates the use of woodland, grazing and haymaking rights, the cutting and fencing of timber in the abbot's woods, and use of an island and adjacent river reaches according to a marked boundary. If people from Borssow damaged Talafus's crops while travelling on the roads, they were to compensate him as assessed by two trustworthy men. Both parties promised faithfully and in good Christian manner to observe the terms. Ulrich and Johann had their seals attached and issued a copy of the agreement to each party.

Given and written at Krumau on Friday, the day of Saint Bartholomew the Apostle, 1453. Two small seals in red wax hang from parchment strips: one bears a shield with a rose and the legend “Sigillum Domini Ulrici de Rozmberg”; the other is similar and bears the legend “S. Jan z Rosenbergka.”
